messages:
Priya Chen: heads-up — ACME (customer id: acct_7f2) opened a ticket saying their nightly sync triggered a bunch of 429s. They say the spike lasted ~60-120s and then kept getting intermittent 429s for the next 10m. They pasted a curl repro and a few headers. Can eng help confirm if this is burst-credit exhaustion vs quota? :wave:

Priya Chen: repro snippet they sent:
```
curl -i \ 
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-acct_7f2\" \ 
  -d '{"input":"...lots of items..."}' \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
They get a 429 with headers: `x-rate-limit-limit: 60`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-rate-limit-reset: 12`, `x-redwood-burst-credits: 0`, `retry-after: 8`

Priya Chen: they are on hosted free-tier with a default route limit of 60 rps. Their sync job runs 400 concurrent requests for ~90s. They expected burst credits but say they ran out.

Samir Patel: thanks — putting context from runtime team. Short answer: sounds like they consumed both their steady-state rate and available burst credits. Our burst model is a token-bucket where burst credits accumulate up to a cap (configured per plan). If the incoming rate exceeds refill rate + burst bucket, requests get 429s with `x-redwood-burst-credits: 0`.

Samir Patel: quick checks I need: (1) customer org id (acct_7f2 ok), (2) route path they used (`/v1/generate` ok), (3) which model variant, (4) any proxy layer on their side doing retries, (5) request body distribution (long vs short).

Janelle Lee: adding SRE notes — our smoothing policy has two levers: burst-cap (max credits) and refill-rate (credits/sec). For free-tier refill-rate ~= 1 credit/sec and burst-cap ~= 120 credits (so ~2 minutes at 60 rps). If they hit 400 rps for 90s, token-bucket empties quickly and then Remaining=0 until refill. That explains the 429s recurring for 10m: they retried aggressively without exponential backoff and kept drawing down the refill.

Janelle Lee: actionable options:
- client-side: implement jitter + exponential backoff and a local leaky-bucket limiter so the sync spreads over time.
- server-side (short-term): grant a one-off temporary burst-topup or bump their route limit for the maintenance window. We can also enable dynamic smoothing that converts short spikes into a queuing window for hosted routes (experimental).

Samir Patel: for the record, math example: they have 120 burst credits + 60/sec refill. If they run 400 rps, net drain = 340 tokens/sec => bucket empties in ~0.35s (120/340). After that they only get refill 60/sec so they can sustain 60 rps; anything above that gets 429. So their expectation that burst covers a 90s plateau was optimistic.

Priya Chen: ok that's helpful — customer claims other providers allowed a 2-minute burst at that scale. Any quick mitigation we can offer while they refactor?

OpsOnCall: I can temporarily increase their burst-cap by +600 credits and set soft limit to 200 rps for 30 minutes from now if we agree. That should absorb the next maintenance window. I'll also add a note to revoke in 1 hour. :white_check_mark:

Samir Patel: +1 to temporary bump, but let's gate it: require customer to confirm exact maintenance start time and agree to client-side backoff changes. We don't want repeated manual bumps. Also log this as a policy exception.

Priya Chen: I'll ask them for start time and share recommended client changes. Also sending them a short doc snippet explaining burst-credit mechanics and header interpretation.

Priya Chen: snippet I'll send them:
```
Interpreting headers:
- x-rate-limit-limit: steady-state allowed rps for the route
- x-rate-limit-remaining: tokens left until steady-state limit reached
- x-rate-limit-reset: seconds until steady-state window reset
- x-redwood-burst-credits: remaining burst tokens in your bucket
- retry-after: how long to wait before retrying (seconds)

If x-redwood-burst-credits is 0 and you are > limit, backoff immediately with jitter. For batch jobs, spread across time or use a concurrency cap.
```

support-bot: Incident-note created: INC-2026-0315-ACME-BURST (assigned to Samir, Janelle). Auto-tag: rate-limit, burst-credit, customer-support.

Janelle Lee: follow-up items for eng: (A) consider adding a clearer `x-redwood-burst-cap` header so customers can see their max bucket size; (B) evaluate a small adaptive queue for hosted routes to smooth very short spikes (<5s) that would otherwise blow the bucket. This would cost modest memory and add small latency but improve UX for sync jobs.

Samir Patel: noted — I'll add A to the runtime backlog and prototype B as an opt-in config for routes.

Priya Chen: customer confirmed start time tomorrow 02:00 UTC and asked for the temp bump. I've scheduled OpsOnCall bump for T-minus 10m before job and will collect logs after. I'll close the ticket once they confirm success.

OpsOnCall: done — I applied +600 credits and soft-limit 200 rps for acct_7f2 at 2026-03-15T01:50:00Z. Will revert at 2026-03-15T02:50:00Z. Monitoring alert set for repeated 429s.

Priya Chen: thanks everyone. I'll post result in this thread after the run. :thumbsup:
